featured_videos.commentary: The community's picking up on something real here. everyone's noticing the *glow*, not just the number on the scale. Fifty pounds is huge, but what's hitting different is Kipp's energy. That's the stuff that doesn't show up in a calculator. When people talk about inflammation going away and the sparkle coming back to their eyes, they're describing something our culture doesn't measure but everyone *feels*. This is why the non-scale victories matter so much, especially early on when the scale might stall or plateau. The mental shift, the way your face changes, how your clothes fit, the energy to actually do things. that's the stuff that keeps people going when the numbers get sticky.

featured_videos.commentary: The comments here tell the real story. People aren't excited about RFK Jr. or the mainstream attention for clout. They're excited because carnivore fixed what nothing else could. IBS that vanished, blurry vision clearing up, yeast infections gone, numb toes coming back to life. That's the pattern we keep seeing, and it matters because Western medicine typically treats these as separate problems requiring separate drugs. But when someone eliminates plants entirely and their whole body starts healing at once, that points to something fundamental about how food actually works in our system. The cultural shift at Meat Stock isn't really about celebrity endorsements. It's about people getting their health back and telling their friends. That's always been the real engine behind this movement.

featured_videos.commentary: Four ingredients and you've got dessert that actually fits a low-carb life. That's the whole appeal here, and the comments show people are ready to actually make this instead of just scrolling past. What strikes me is how simple Patricia keeps it, eggs and cocoa and sweetener, none of the complicated substitutions that usually derail home cooks. If you're dealing with those 3pm sweet cravings without wanting to derail your macros, this hits different than reaching for something with flour and sugar. The protein density matters too. six grams per serving isn't accidental, it's the whole point of building a dessert that actually sustains you instead of spiking your blood sugar and leaving you hungry an hour later.
